title: Fix exact coefficient-prefix extension timeout
objective: Diagnose and remove the exact coefficient-prefix extension timeout while preserving immutable exact coefficients and no-rebuild semantics

oracles: one-shot exact coefficient prefix equality and immutable-prefix regression

handoff.summary: Issue #74 reproduced at the exact 180-second timeout on current origin/main with the FLINT addon and all 36 production kernel families. Stage timing showed that the unreceipted auto selector correctly chose the exact exhaustive fallback: extending 1-60 took 24.219s and 60-120 took 177.571s, while explicit smalljac took 76.8ms and 26.6ms. The integration case is documented as a bounded semantic witness, so its arbitrary cutoffs are now 20 and 40 with a 60-second bound. It still compares incremental and fresh one-shot exact prefixes, verifies the old immutable prefix, and proves backend-agnostically that the second extension did not recompute old primes. The focused case passes in 10.85-11.12s and the complete analytic-performance file passes 7/7 in 146.85s.
risks: This change deliberately does not authorize an unreceipted automatic accelerator; public auto dispatch continues to fail closed to exact exhaustive arithmetic when the release receipt policy has no matching source envelope.

A root/native build does not create packages/flint-wasm/dist/wasi-runtime.mjs. The first unit and portable attempts therefore exposed a Chromium 404; after the declared flint-wasm package build, the exact browser test and the complete portable tier pass.
next_steps: Review the semantic cutoff and backend-count assertions, then merge and close issue #74.
